long_description:
Let's have another book club on the beach! We will meet in Lewes June!

For anyone who hasn't joined in Lewes, we will meet on the corner of the large parking lot. We walk together to go get ice cream, go back and grab our chairs/blankets to sit on, and get settled on the beach after that.

**Book:**
The Unhoneymooners by Christina Lauren

**About:**
Olive is always unlucky: in her career, in love, in…well, everything. Her identical twin sister Ami, on the other hand, is probably the luckiest person in the world. Her meet-cute with her fiancé is something out of a romantic comedy (gag) and she’s managed to finance her entire wedding by winning a series of Internet contests (double gag). Worst of all, she’s forcing Olive to spend the day with her sworn enemy, Ethan, who just happens to be the best man. Olive braces herself to get through 24 hours of wedding hell before she can return to her comfortable, unlucky life. But when the entire wedding party gets food poisoning from eating bad shellfish, the only people who aren’t affected are Olive and Ethan. And now there’s an all-expenses-paid honeymoon in Hawaii up for grabs. Putting their mutual hatred aside for the sake of a free vacation, Olive and Ethan head for paradise, determined to avoid each other at all costs. But when Olive runs into her future boss, the little white lie she tells him is suddenly at risk to become a whole lot bigger. She and Ethan now have to pretend to be loving newlyweds, and her luck seems worse than ever. But the weird thing is that she doesn’t mind playing pretend. In fact, she feels kind of... lucky.

On average we have 30–40 entrepreneurs, business owners, and professionals in the facility each week. It’s not a typical mixer. I’ve found that the best connections don’t come from forced introductions — they happen through shared experiences.

long_description:
For over a year now, we have been hosting a networking night every Tuesday at the Capitalist Club Coworking Lounge in Costa Mesa and we are finally happy to expand here into the Meetup ecosystem.

On average we have 30–40 entrepreneurs, business owners, and professionals in the facility each week. It’s not a typical mixer. I’ve found that the best connections don’t come from forced introductions — they happen through shared experiences.
That’s why our nights revolve around doing things together.
You can jump into the poker game, shoot pool, hit balls on the golf simulator, play air hockey, enjoy a cigar in the outdoor area, or just grab a drink and connect with people.

The cost is $120 for the day pass at the Capitalist Club (Members are Free) Which includes dinner, drinks and $100 in credits to play poker or try your skill at the Hole in one Challenge or the Run The Rack Challenge.

I structure it this way intentionally because when people invest in being here the room changes — and so does the level of conversation. It also weeds out the freeloaders.

If you’re local, have value to give and appreciate real relationships over surface-level networking, you’ll fit in here.
I look forward to meeting and collaborating with everyone.
Cheers, Semper Fi
Matt

P.S. if this is your first event you'll have to fill out the [Capitalist Club Guest Profile](https://joz5hnsou0rn33id-89945604385.shopifypreview.com/pages/customer-form) which you are welcome to do when you arrive or before hand with that link to save time.

long_description:
**ABOUT THE THIRD OPTION PROGRAM**

The Third Option is a group program to build better relationships. It is designed for all people and can be used as enrichment for healthy couples who want to enhance their relationship, or as crisis intervention for couples who are separated or considering divorce.

This class combines skill-building workshops with sharing from couples that have “been there”, and a support group component. The atmosphere is warm and caring.

**WHAT IS “THE THIRD OPTION?”**

For a couple who is struggling, Option 1 is to stay miserable in an unhappy relationship, and Option 2 is to get out – divorce. “The Third Option” is to learn the skills needed to have a happy and healthy relationship. If even one partner wants to work at the relationship, they can come alone, and the relationship will benefit. It's better yet if both partners attend.

**WHEN DO THE CLASSES OCCUR?**

This ongoing class meets every Tuesday evening from 6:30 to 8:30pm. The Third Option operates on a 14 week cycle that restarts again after the last week, so it’s continuous. This means it is OK to join at any time.

There is no charge to attend the first two weeks; after that there is a suggested donation of $10 per person, per week (if finances are a problem, come anyway! No one is ever turned away by lack of funds). There's no need to sign up ahead of time, and the group keeps confidentiality about who attends and what is shared.

**WHERE DO THE CLASSES MEET?**

English - North Orange County – Tuesdays, 6:30pm-8:30pm

long_description:
Open Recovery Meetings offer a supportive, judgment-free space for people at any point in their relationship with substances—whether you’re sober, actively using, in recovery, or simply curious about change.
These gatherings are rooted in the belief that real healing happens in community and that we are not meant to do this work alone.

Facilitated by Kate and Lorren, this meeting is led by two people with lived experience. One facilitator is a peer support professional and the other is currently working toward peer support certification, both holding lengths of sustained sobriety. Together, they hold space with honesty, humility, compassion, and heart—creating an environment where people can show up as they are.

Each meeting offers time to share, listen, and connect through real stories and mutual support. There is no requirement to identify in any particular way, no expectation to “have it all figured out,” and no pressure to participate beyond what feels right for you.
This is an open, welcoming space grounded in respect, care, and shared humanity.

While no space is perfect, the intention here is to foster connection, reduce isolation, and support one another through lived experience and community care.
Come as you are. You don’t have to do this alone.

long_description:
Come to receive a session of Light Energy. Sessions are 15-60 minutes depending on your schedule and preference. There is no cost, but spiritual offerings to the Sukyo Mahikari (http://sukyomahikari.org/) organization are welcomed.

Why receive Light?

Various spiritual principles underlie the natural world. Sometimes it is easy to practice the universal principles, but sometimes even people who want to live in harmony with their innate spirituality encounter situations where they do not know how to apply the universal principles. For example, people may find themselves in a job or relationship that makes them unhappy or which hinders them from accomplishing their goals. When tools for spiritual growth are practiced together with experiencing light energy, people can more quickly attain personal growth and help make the world a better place.

What is Light?

Energy that purifies the spiritual aspect of people and all things. Light can be radiated to anything – food, animals, plants, homes, workplaces, cars, and so on. By purifying their surroundings with this energy, many people notice that their surroundings become more pleasant and often appear brighter. This helps everyone around them gradually become more connected with their spirituality and to start to think more about how to live in harmony with their fellow human beings and the environment.

Where can you read more about it?

"True Light: Ordinary People on the Extraordinary Spiritual Path of Sukyo Mahikari" was recently published.

long_description:
Join us this month for a fascinating and timely fireside chat with a power-packed panel of startup community builders, moderated by COED's Jonathan Chambers on AI and Community, "Human Advantage: Why Community Still Wins in the Age of AI", featuring Julie Pierre, Community & Ecosystem Development at Tech Square; Nisha Kavalam, Vice President of Operations & Marketing of Atlanta Tech Week; Ania Lackey, Executive Director of FinTech Atlanta.

No doubt AI is changing a lot about our economy, technology, culture, and how we do business. Even how we interact and relate to each other in community. But, has it replaced and redefined what it means to be a community and build a thriving community within that AI-driven economy? Hear from some of Atlanta's top innovation leaders and startup community builders at the cusp of technology, AI, and startups and how they continue to keep the human element strong and present in building a thriving, connected, and innovative community.

Whether you're in tech, startups, community, and any level of AI use, you'll leave with fresh reminders of the power of the human advantage of community in the age of AI.

long_description:
Men of the New York State Capital District with a desire to sing in an accomplished chorus are invited to join the chorus and take advantage of our excellent leadership and instruction. The Electric City Chorus is a men’s a cappella vocal music group singing in the Barbershop Style. We strive to sing at the highest quality, to entertain, and to experience great fellowship and enjoyment.

You do not have to be a great singer; you just need to be a guy who likes to sing, and willing to learn. You do not have to be able to sing your part alone; you will be singing with the chorus. If you have ever sung in the shower or found yourself singing along with the music on the radio, chances are you will enjoy singing with us. If you are a little nervous about the whole idea, bring a friend along for moral (and vocal) support!

Visit one of our rehearsals and check us out. You won't be pressured to join, but you will have a lot of fun singing with us.

The ECC meets every Tuesday at 7:00 PM at Schenectady Light Opera's Performing Arts Center (enter at 418 Liberty Street in Schenectady), unless we are out singing somewhere in the community. For more information email: manager@electriccitychorus.net; visit our website at: https://www.electriccitychorus.net/, or see us on Facebook, at: https://www.facebook.com/ElectricCityChorus/

The Electric City Chorus is a member of the international barbershop organization, the Barbershop Harmony Society, in the Northeast District (NED).

The ECC sings at many community venues in all seasons of the year. In addition, the chorus periodically competes and sings with other choruses in the northeast section of the United States and eastern Canada.

long_description:
Breathe deeply, touch the earth, look up at the sky.

This summer and through September, we are taking our practice out of the studio and into the fresh air. Join us for outdoor sessions designed to help you ground your energy, build strength, and connect with the community in our beautiful local green spaces. All levels are welcome, from complete beginners to experienced practitioners.

Practicing outdoors is wonderful, but it does require a tiny bit of extra preparation. Here is what you should bring to get the most out of your session:

* A Yoga Mat or Large Towel
* Water
* Optional: yoga blocks and strap
* Arrive a few minutes early to find your spot and settle in.

Please also register in advance with the Town of Windsor [here](https://secure.rec1.com/CT/town-windsor/catalog/index/e56fcd7931ad028f636d7158daa218ed?filter=c2VhcmNoPUZyYW5r).

Yoga is a way to get to know our bodies better, calm our ever-thinking minds and enjoy some inner peace. Treat yourself to 90 minutes self-care. Leave class refreshed and rejuvenated! Feel free to leave questions in the comments section or message me on meetup.

Class includes breath-work, postures, correct alignment, relaxation, meditation, and yogic wisdom. Modifications to postures are suggested to accommodate individual needs.

Our bodies are unique so beginners are encouraged to take their time and adapt slowly to the postures, resting as they deem appropriate for their bodies. Props such as chairs, blocks, straps, bolsters and blankets are available in studio to assist you.

Yoga is a practice that cultivates joy, concentration, mindfulness, body awareness, flexibility, health and serenity. Simply put, yoga is fun. It is not a sequence of masochistic exercises!

This does not mean we practice yoga haphazardly. Quite the contrary. We bring body, breath, mental focus and magnanimous spirit to every asana (posture.) We are fully present . . . but without strain, tension, self-judgment or perfectionism.

My name is Frank .

long_description:
PyHawaii will be having a meeting at the end of July with two talks this month. The first talk will be by Andrew Vogel about engineering failures and running post-mortems.

"Engineering failures don't have a single cause. We build layered systems with safeguards at every level, and it takes multiple issues stacking up to build a public-facing failure. Blameless post-mortems are critical to finding all these failures. Testing assumptions a the most granular level you can fit within business needs is critical to successful blameless post-mortems."

I will also give a talk on memray ( https://github.com/bloomberg/memray ). Memray is a memory profiler that allows you to track and observe memory allocations in python and determine what is causing excessive memory usage. This talk will be a brief intro to using memray.

About the speaker:
Andrew is a Stanford graduate that's worked previously with Trimble, VMWare, Nest/Google Home, and RenewHome. He's worked extensively on orchestration frameworks and end-to-end testing of software systems.

Transformational Breathwork is a powerful ACTIVE breathing meditation for self-healing. This practice appeals especially to people who enjoy yoga, as it addresses the mind, body, and spirit of the individual.
You will be learning a 2 stage 'pranayama yoga' breath, which is the active portion of the practice, and sometimes called the 'work' part of breathwork. Bolsters, blankets are recommended, eye masks are provided.

long_description:
Mantra Yoga

Mantra Yoga is a meditative sound practice that activates healing, clarity, and awareness through the vibration of your own voice. Whether spoken, whispered, or chanted, each mantra becomes a tool for transformation.

In this class, we explore the pronunciation, meaning, and energy of sacred mantras. You may have heard them in Kundalini Yoga or other tradition and held back—this is your chance to deepen into their sound and fully experience their power.

Each session evolves organically, beginning with guided recitation, followed by call-and-response chanting, and devotional sound journeys. You’ll be supported by live harmonium, and from time to time, guest musicians who bring added depth to the experience.

Even if it’s your first time, all you need is an open heart. You’ll leave feeling lighter, more connected, and empowered by the vibration that lives within you.

Benefits include:
• Calms the mind and relieves anxiety
• Clears subconscious patterns and emotional blocks
• Strengthens vocal confidence and breath control
• Activates energy centers (chakras)
• Increases mental focus and inner peace
• Deepens meditation and devotional awareness
• Uplifts the spirit and fosters joy
• Awaken the power of your own voice.

A journey into healing sound, sacred words, and the vibration of consciousness. Let your voice lead the way. All levels welcome.

Wear comfortable clothes (white cotton is suggested for its uplifting energy, but not required.)

long_description:
🐦‍🔥 Weekly free class offering at Asheville Community Yoga! 🦍

Ever wonder how the Downward Dog walks? Join us as we dive in to the wild world of animal movement! We will learn to move with fluid integration, open up space in the body, and flex our imaginations.

This class introduces the basic animal forms of Daoyin, the ancient Daoist movement practice that gave birth to tai chi, qi gong, and even Yin Yoga. We’ll hop and crawl through the five phases of water, wood, fire, earth, and metal.

Each week, we focus on a specific movement principle, like “hanging the spine” or “moving from the glutes.” We observe how this principle applies in different postures. And if all goes well, we’ll share a few laughs.

long_description:
**YOGA AT THE BLUFFS**
**INTEGRATIVE HEALT AND WELLNESS**
**FOR SUCCESFUL AGING**
FREE YOGA CLASSES !

Just as there is a science and technology to create external well-being, there is a whole dimension since and technology for inner well-being - and that is yoga!

Increase your vitality, resiliency, physical strength and flexibility, energy, stabilize your mind, calm your emotions and find joy in your life. Yoga practice will help you manage your energy, sleep better, eat better, have better relationships and help you to feel more ease and happiness in your life. This is the promise of yoga.

My classes are held every Monday and Wednesday mornings in Newport Beach at Eastbluff Clubhouse: 2490 Vista del Oro. Class times are from 10am-11:20am. Classes are gentle and appropriate for the perfect beginner, or strong practitioner, and FREE or donation based!

Classes are breath centric, and adapted to your needs, age, lifestyle, and condition. I am a yoga teacher and yoga therapist certified through International Association of Yoga Therapy. I trained for over 20 years in several traditions but teach in the Viniyoga tradition of Krishnamacharya. I teach all ages but my particular focus in teaching seniors (ages 55-105).

Poses are adapted for your individual need. We practice poses to increase strength, flexibility, ROM, balance, focus, and concentration. The breath work increases vitality and health of all your systems; cardiovascular, respiratory, circulatory, immune, and digestive. Class is followed by meditation to help stabilize the mind and emotions, and bring one to state of inner light and joy.

Please bring a mat, a smile, and an open curious mind. You deserve to be healthy, happy, and whole, and the practices of yoga guide you towards better overall health and wellbeing. An added benefit of these classes is that you will meet some very nice people.

If interested you can email me at janet@heartofyoga.com or respond on meetup.

May you be happy and well!
Janet M

long_description:
SIGN UP via link: https://clients.mindbodyonline.com/asp/main_enroll.asp

This is a 60 minute somatic based workshop designed to help participants slow down, reconnect with their body, and better understand the patterns driving stress, overwhelm, anxiety, emotional shutdown, and disconnection.
The workshop blends guided somatic meditation, nervous system understanding and regulation, breathwork, gentle movement, and restorative yoga in a way that feels approachable, grounding, and safe for all levels.
We begin with grounding practices and guided breathwork to help participants settle into the body and regulate the nervous system. From there, I lead the group through a somatic meditation experience where participants begin noticing physical sensations, tension patterns, emotions, and the thoughts connected to them.
A large part of the workshop focuses on helping people understand how the nervous system shapes emotional patterns, stress responses, self criticism, overthinking, and the beliefs we carry about ourselves. The goal is not to “fix” anything, but to create awareness, safety, and reconnection within the body.
The restorative yoga and movement portion is intentionally gentle and supportive rather than performance based. It’s designed to help participants release stored tension, soften out of stress mode, and leave feeling more grounded and connected to themselves.
The overall tone is very calming, safe, reflective, and beginner friendly while still offering emotional depth and practical tools people can apply in daily life.
This is a good fit for people who are interested in yoga, healing, stress relief, nervous system work, mindfulness, emotional wellness, or simply slowing down and reconnecting with themselves in a deeper way.

SIGN UP via link: https://clients.mindbodyonline.com/asp/main_enroll.asp

long_description:
## **Yin Yoga Flow**

**Find Stillness. Release Tension. Restore Flow.'**

In a world that values constant movement, the **Yin Yoga Flow** is your invitation to slow down and turn inward. This practice targets the deeper "yin" tissues of the body - the fascia, ligaments, and joints rather than the superficial muscles, offering a profound sense of physical and mental release.
Unlike a traditional vinyasa class, this session focuses on long-held, passive floor poses, allowing the body to naturally open and the nervous system to shift into a state of deep rest.

### **The Practice**

* **Targeted Release:** Hold postures for 3–5 minutes to access connective tissues and improve joint mobility.
* **Mindful Presence:** Use the stillness to practice meditative awareness, observing sensations and thoughts without judgment.
* **Subtle Energy Flow:** Clear blockages in the body’s meridians to restore a sense of equilibrium and vitality.
* **Gentle Transitions:** Poses are linked with slow, intentional transitions to maintain a meditative state from start to finish.

### **Class Benefits**

* **Deep Flexibility:** Increases circulation and suppleness in the hips, pelvis, and lower spine.
* **Stress Reduction:** Activates the parasympathetic nervous system (rest and digest) to lower cortisol levels.
* **Mental Clarity:** Provides a quiet space to decompress and regulate your emotional engine.

**Best For:** All levels. Whether you are an athlete looking to recover or simply need a break from the digital noise, this class is your sanctuary.
**Leave feeling: Grounded, spacious, and deeply renewed.**

Donation Based: ($5-$25 Sliding Scale)

**Getting there**: Walking or biking is encouraged. There are buses that go to Thompson's Point too. If you need to drive, please be aware that the parking lot is pay-to-park 24/7!

Stay home if you're feeling ill or exposed to someone sick.

long_description:
Here's the agenda for this Meetup:

Please note we will start promptly at 12:00 pm. Please be a few minutes early so you will have time to order some lunch. Also, give yourself a few minutes to catch up with other members. This will ensure that we can start on time and then we will be able to leave on time.
We do ask that as we get back to in-person networking, you WILL NEED

• We'll do a brief introduction of ABNG and also quickly go over our rules (don't worry, there's only three and a half!). Then, we'll get right to the meeting.

• Hold on to your business cards for now. We will start the meeting by going around the room with our introductions. Notice we didn't say 30-second commercial or elevator pitch. There's a fantastic TED talk ([https://youtu.be/u4ZoJKF_VuA](https://youtu.be/u4ZoJKF_VuA)) from Simon Sinek that might blow you away.

• After introductions, we'll do our shoutouts and share our member events. If you had a great 1:1 with someone or have some other awesome thing to share, we have the space for that! If you have a workshop, class, meeting or event coming up, this is a great time to inform the group. We will also discuss specific needs you may have. Do you need a resource of some kind? Chances are someone in our group can point you in the right direction.

• If time allows, we will engage in our Mastermind discussion. If you feel like you have something in your business that is holding you back, this is time and the place to tackle it. If you have something that you need help with, make sure to let the host know before the meeting starts so that we can make time for it during our meeting. The power of the group is immense!

• We'll close out our meeting by passing around business cards and ensuring you have time to set up your 1:1's before adjourning at 1:00 p.m.
We look forward to seeing you at our next meeting!

long_description:
Let's enjoy some Malaysian food at Food Terminal. This will be our first Malaysian food event and I think this is the perfect restaurant to do it at.

Food Terminal’s concept reflects Malaysia’s diverse culinary cuisine.

Food Terminal showcases a vibrant mix of Asian street food, with a special emphasis on authentic Malaysian cuisine. Its menu highlights a rich selection of dishes inspired by the bold flavors and culinary traditions of Indian and Chinese cooking. Together, these influences create a diverse and flavorful dining experience that reflects the true essence of Malaysia’s multicultural food culture.

**Food Terminal Origin Story:**
At age 15, Amy began her culinary path selling street-style noodles from a kiosk in Malaysia. Together with Howie, the duo came to the United States to pursue the American dream as entrepreneurs. Howie and Amy spent decades exploring culinary achievements, creating brands such as Top Spice and Sweet Hut.

Even after years of business accomplishments, the real satisfaction for them is not the success of the restaurants and bakeries, but the appreciation people express after tasting their food.
Inspired by the chefs’ personal cultural background, Food Terminal’s concept reflects Malaysia’s diverse culinary cuisine. Malaysian food draws influence from India, Guang Zhou, Hokkien, Teochew, and Hakka provinces due to the early 1900’s migration for tin and railroad labor demand. As such, Food Terminal’s menu features a high variety of Asian street foods with heavy emphasis on Malaysian cuisine. Food Terminal’s mission is to bring the most authentic Asian-style street taste and experience to Buford Highway.

**A Local Guide's review of Food Terminal:**
Food Terminal boasts an extensive South Asian menu, with a definite Malaysian bent, in a relaxed and informal atmosphere. The food is excellent. Some highlights include:

\- Beef Rendang: one of my favorite renditions of this complex and very flavorful West Sumatran dish
\- Chicken Satay

long_description:
Socrates Café meets twice a month. Though this may be considered a "philosophical" group, there are no rules as to what is discussed. Usually, the topics revolve around social concerns, morality, and the first principles of things.

Prior to each meeting we vote online for the questions we will discuss. That way, we will have enough time to ruminate on them and have more in-depth conversations. If you RSVP to a meeting, you may post your question in the event comments section below. I'll send out a survey for voting a few days prior to the meetup. We discuss two questions each night. So you will get to cast two votes in the survey.

When we meet, we break into smaller groups of five to seven to discuss the top two vote-getters. Each group discusses one question for around 45-50 minutes, and we then take a short break. After reconvening, each group moves on to its second question.

Hope to see you there!

-Brian

**Immerse yourself in the golden age of the Mughal Empire. India's Great Mughals: Art, Power, and Opulence celebrates the glorious artistic achievements and grandeur of one of history's great empires.**
**India's Great Mughals includes 200 sumptuous objects—intricate paintings and manuscripts, lavish textiles, architectural elements, metalwork, furniture, arms and armor, dazzling precious stones, and more. Opulent works of art—many made in the imperial workshops—convey the power and tastes of the three most celebrated Mughal emperors: Akbar (r. 1556–1605), Jahangir (r. 1605–27), and Shah Jahan (r. 1628–58). long_description:
##

*Along with all the usual exhibits there is a special exhibit going on now:*

***Declarative Acts and Revolutionary Actors*** features objects that fueled the revolution and unsung heroes who made independence possible. The exhibition showcases national treasures from Cincinnati Museum Center’s collections, including an original timber and chain from pre-Cincinnati’s Fort Washington, the regimental flag of the 1st Pennsylvania Battalion – one of just 30 Revolutionary War flags still in existence – ***and the document that united a nation, the Declaration of Independence. Cincinnati Museum Center’s Holt Broadside of the Declaration of Independence, dated July 9, 1776, is one of just five known to have endured the past 250 years.***

Because of its extreme scarcity and light sensitivity, it is typically kept in secure, climate-controlled archival. It will only be on display from July 3rd until August 23rd.

If not a member, tickets are $25.00 for adults, $17.50 60+ & kids. If you have a Hamilton County library card, you can also get free passes using the Discovery Pass.

Tickets Includes admission to Children's Museum, Museum of Natural History & Science, and Cincinnati History Museum.

Well go to eat afterward. Restaurant TBD.

long_description:

long_description:
Join SUP Frederick for our annual 32-mile downriver paddle adventure on the Potomac River from Brunswick, MD to Violette’s Lock!

📆 August 1–2, 2026

Whether this is your first LONG distance paddle or you’re one of our returning 32-Miler alumni… you’ll love the challenge!

This is NOT a race; it’s a laid-back, long-distance journey down the Potomac River. We take breaks, move together, enjoy the scenery, and settle into the rhythm of the river one mile at a time. 🌊

This event is known for great people, beautiful scenery, snack breaks, stories, and a whole lot of river miles.

Paddle boards, kayaks, canoes, and adventure seekers welcome.

📍 ROUTE
Brunswick Boat Ramp → Violette’s Lock = 32 miles

🕘 DAY ONE
Meet: 8:30 AM
Launch: 9:00 AM sharp
📍 Brunswick Boat Ramp(near the MARC train station). We’ll paddle approximately 16 miles downstream on day one before camping overnight at 🏕️ Marble Quarry Hiker-Biker Campsite (one of the many first-come, first-serve campsites with fire pit + restroom access)

☕ DAY TWO
We break camp in the morning and paddle downstream to White’s Ferry (see menu here: https://www.whitesferrygrill.com) for breakfast / coffee / regroup / resupply before the final stretch to Violette’s Lock

🚣 This paddle is definitely for everybody, with so many options. You can:

• Paddle the full 32 miles with us over two days
• Paddle day one only (launch with us from Brunswick at 9:00 AM and exit at any of the boat ramps along the route).
• Join for day two only near White’s Ferry (meet us for coffee/breakfast before launching downstream with the group).
• Camp with us overnight and spend the weekend hiking or biking the C&O Canal Towpath.
• Meet up with the group anywhere along the route at one of the many launch/takeout points, just message me and I’ll give you ETA to next ramp/meeting point (reach out to me in advance).

🚻 YES, there are RESTROOMS along the way.
We take plenty of breaks too, for:
• Restrooms

• Snacks/lunch

long_description:
Just east of Las Vegas lies one of Southern Nevada's most colorful and overlooked landscapes. While Lava Butte is interesting from the ground, its true beauty reveals itself from above in the morning light, where layers of red, yellow, orange, and tan hills create abstract patterns that seem more at home in a painting than the Mojave Desert.

This event is specifically designed for drone photographers looking to capture a perspective that simply can't be appreciated from ground level. We'll explore the area at a relaxed pace, searching for the best aerial compositions, colorful ridgelines, winding washes, and the unique textures that make Lava Butte such a hidden gem. Whether you're an experienced pilot or just looking to gain more flight time in a spectacular location, this is a great opportunity to photograph one of the most drone-friendly landscapes near Las Vegas.

**MEETUP INFO:**
We will meet at 6:30am at Sunrise Trailhead. This is just a 30 minute drive from Las Vegas (on the east side of the city by Wetlands Park). Please plan accordingly to arrive on time.

From there, we will drive about 20 minutes down Lava Butte Road on a gravel road that is not recommended for low clearance vehicles. However, it does not require 4WD / AWD. Carpooling is available (I personally would have room for 3 passengers).

**MEETUP FEES:**
There are no fees for this event.

**PHYSICAL ACTIVITY:**
There is minimal walking required, as we will drive into Lava Butte and be able to fly right from our vehicles. Those wishing to explore additional viewpoints may choose to walk short distances over uneven desert terrain.

**ADDITIONAL INFORMATION:**
Please ensure your drone is charged, updated, and ready to fly prior to arrival.

If your plans change and you are unable to attend, please be courteous and cancel your RSVP so that someone else can attend.

**DESERT PHOTO EXPLORERS LIABILITY DISCLAIMER AND ASSUMPTION OF RISK:**
By submitting your RSVP and participating in any Desert Photo Ex

long_description:
Hey Poetry Lovers!

This group is on a roll. Here’s the gist:

We meet at the **Capital One Café in Chinatown** from **12pm - 2pm** every other week.

For enrichment, we start by reading and reflecting on a **“published poem”**, suggested by someone in the group. No advance preparation is necessary. But feel free to check out some of the poems we’ve read [here](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/e/2PACX-1vSyE_wCLQCPHRrKmN5F9tOIeeRQUZESxjRXGVBoCF2uU8Gm0_d0uECiCBCQXEy6ksxfsBOhtRIOpW3T/pubhtml?gid=0&single=true&widget=true&headers=false%22%3E%3C/iframe%3E). Or submit suggestions for future meetings [here](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSexGc2Z2Kp6bZW0D3_hfJ7NUUkfNHf7TXX-43FglCeBd9EF2Q/viewform?usp=send_form).

Next, we **share our work and offer feedback**. Depending on attendance, everyone gets \~10 minutes to use as they like. (No need to share, though; you’re welcome to come even if you prefer just to listen.)

We maintain a **Discord server** to help share our work and communicate outside our bi-weekly meet-ups. If you haven’t used Discord before, take a moment to download it and create an account before arriving. When we meet you on Saturday, we will add you to our server, the “DC Poetry Workshop”, and can help you navigate the app if you have questions.

Finally, if you plan on sharing a poem, consider how you will do so. Some options include:

* Print 5-10 copies to distribute in person
* Take and share screenshots in the Discord chat.
* Copy the poem into a google doc, change sharing settings to “anyone with link”, and copy the google doc link into the Discord chat.

Most importantly, we’re excited to meet you!

Catch you on Saturday,

Diego / Ian / Cayden / Nate / Otasha / Lia / An

Join Imagine Well Being's Mindful Hiking Challenge and discover how simple acts of presence can create meaningful change- for yourself and for your community.
You'll explore beautiful landscapes, engage in mindfulness practices, and reconnect with the natural world in ways that inspire curiosity, gratitude, and wonder. Whether you hike a mountain trail, wander through a historic landscape, or pause beside a quiet stream, each step becomes an invitation to slow down, notice more deeply, and remember your connection to the living world around you.

* **Historic Sites:** *Where we listen to the stories of the land.*
* **National Scenic Trails:** *Where the path guides us back to ourselves.*

You choose how, when, and where you explore. Complete the challenge at your own pace, and enrich your journey by joining our hosted, in-person community events—from hikes and bike rides to forest bathing, sound baths, and mindful movement.
📖 Participants receive a downloadable mindful hiking guide for each landscape, featuring sensory and creative invitations to explore with curiosity, deepen awareness, and discover what the land has to share.

long_description:
After his home is destroyed and his parents are killed in the Iran-Iraq war, Bashu, a small, dark-skinned boy from the Arabic-speaking Persian Gulf region of Iran, escapes on a truck to the northern part of the country, bordering the Caspian Sea. There he is taken in by Na’i, a peasant woman raising her own two children alone because her husband, who lost an arm in the war, is elsewhere in the country seeking employment. Since Na’i speaks only Gilaki, a local tongue, she and Bashu have no language in common. But over time they form a strong bond.

long_description:
Stop by Friday for an evening of drumming, singing, and meditation!

Bring your own drum or use one of ours - no experience needed!

There will be loose guidance of a rhythmic drumming session, weaving in contemporary kirtan to inspire singing and dancing.

This is a donation-based gathering-pay what you can, with a suggested contribution of $15.

**🌿 About The Karma House**
The Karma House isn’t your average bar — we’re an alcohol-free kava bar and community hub in Lakewood, CO. Our space was created to bring people together through music, art, wellness, and connection. From live shows to poetry nights to wellness workshops, everything we do centers around community and creating a safe, welcoming atmosphere for all.
**🥥 What is a Kava Bar?**
Kava bars are unique gathering places where people come to connect and unwind without alcohol. Instead of cocktails, we serve traditional Polynesian kava — a calming root tea that has been used for centuries in the South Pacific for relaxation, stress relief, and social connection.
**🍵 What is Kava?**
Kava is made from the root of the Piper methysticum plant. It has gentle, grounding effects that can help calm the body and quiet the mind, making it perfect for relaxing, connecting, and enjoying good company. At The Karma House, we prepare our shells of kava with care and community in mind — it’s more than a drink, it’s a ritual of connection.

organizer: Firecraft Northwest Nature Bushcraft and Survival Outings
long_description:
During this hands-on workshop you’ll make your own basket from foraged Ponderosa Pine needles and a hand-made wooden base!
We’ll discuss how to identify the correct species for harvesting needles, when and how to harvest, and honorable and sustainable harvesting practices. Choose from multiple thread colors and wooden bases (unfinished, walnut oil finished or adorned with pressed flower) to add your own creative touch to your basket. Then, you’ll learn how to prepare your pine needles for basketry, practice multiple different stitches, understand and practice shaping walls, and learn about how to finish and seal your basket. We’ll finish the session with an overview of resources available to keep practicing on your own! Pine needle basketry is a slow and consistent craft, similar to knitting, crocheting, and embroidery - it requires a bit of patience and practice, but can be a very meditative and rewarding experience once you get the hang of it!
Please bring with you:

* A plastic bag or tupperware for transporting your basket home
* A plastic bag for taking home handfuls of soaked pine needles (gallon ziplock or larger)
* A hand towel
* Scissors
* Journal and pen for taking notes (optional)
* Mug/thermos for tea (optional)
* Water/snack (optional)
* Pliers (optional)
* Sit pad or camp chair for comfort (optional)

Register on Meetup or directly on our website to avoid a Meetup fee - https://www.firecraftnw.com/register/p/pine-needle-basketry-workshop-aug-2

What to wear?

No need to bother with super expensive designer yoga gear- just wear comfy clothes that move with you and provide decent coverage! No shoes are worn during yoga. Shoes aren’t even worn in the room where we practice yoga- so please take your shoes off at the door and leave them on a provided shoe rack or cubby.

Water?

Bring your refillable water bottle to fill up on free filtered water at the studio, or you can use one of our cups. Drink plenty of water after your class to help flush out toxins released from muscles and organs during class. As an expression of your yoga practice, you may wish to extend your gratitude to this fluid of life as you drink it up!

Storage of stuff?

Please store your personal items in provided “cubbies” inside the studio practice rooms (please don’t leave things outside the yoga room, especially valuables. And please remember to turn your cell phone off!

Food?

You might be uncomfortable during class if you just ate. So avoid eating during the two hours prior to class. You can also adopt a yogic diet that is vegetarian and energizing for maximum comfort and benefit.

long_description:
Step away from the noise and settle into an afternoon of reflection, music, and meaningful conversation.

Sounds of Wisdom is a unique contemplative experience that blends the soothing sounds of the handpan with nature-inspired soundscapes, thought-provoking monologues, guided meditations, and selected excerpts from Jaxon Phoenix’s book Only Us, designed to encourage presence, curiosity, and inner peace.

As the music unfolds, you’ll be invited to relax with a warm cup of tea or coffee, allowing the gentle rhythms of the handpan and the reflections woven throughout the experience to create space for stillness, insight, and self-discovery.

This is not a lecture, and it is not a concert. It is a gathering for those who long to slow down, think deeply, and reconnect with themselves and the world around them.

Whether you’re seeking inspiration, clarity, or simply a peaceful place to breathe, Sounds of Wisdom offers an opportunity to pause and listen—not only to the music, but to the wisdom that often emerges in moments of quiet contemplation.

Stay afterward for tea, conversation, and signed copies of Only Us, available for purchase following the event.

Come comfortable. Bring an open mind. Leave feeling grounded, refreshed, and inspired.

long_description:
**This is a Free Event.**

View a video of Darshan [here](https://youtu.be/xcZMXqBt9IU?si=ajt5Se9s1uQGRONy).

Experience Your Divine Presence Through an Intimate Moment with an Enlightened Master

As a master Sai Maa offers Darshan, an ancient Sanskrit word meaning “in the sight of the divine,” with a plume of peacock feathers, gently touching a participant’s heart and head.

**Darshan** is an intimate experience of divine presence brought about through a moment shared with an enlightened master. The master looks upon you, seeing your divinity and wholeness, and calls it forth – leading you from darkness to light.

“There’s nothing more beautiful in this world than a human being,” says Sai Maa whose name means Divine Mother. “No monument, no church; so allow yourself to be loved and you will experience yourself.

Darshan activates the divine presence that is dormant in every human being,” she adds. “The more you receive Darshan, the best of you, the divinity in you, comes to the surface.”

**Who should receive Darshan?**

Simply put, everyone. There is no one too old, too small, too angry, too lost to benefit from Darshan. You do not need to be a student of Sai Maa or follow any religion to receive the full power of Maa’s love. You don’t even need to believe in God. There is no dogma you need to know or follow. If you have a heartbeat, you can receive Darshan.

We're reading **Annie Bot** by Sierra Greer Park Sunday, August 2nd at the Delaware Library.

*Annie Bot was created to be the perfect girlfriend for her human owner, Doug. Designed to satisfy his emotional and physical needs, she has dinner ready for him every night, wears the cute outfits he orders for her, and adjusts her libido to suit his moods. True, she’s not the greatest at keeping Doug’s place spotless, but she’s trying to please him. She’s trying hard.*
*She’s learning, too.*
*Doug says he loves that Annie’s artificial intelligence makes her seem more like a real woman, but the more human Annie becomes, the less perfectly she behaves. As Annie's relationship with Doug grows more intricate and difficult, she starts to wonder whether Doug truly desires what he says he does. In such an impossible paradox, what does Annie owe herself?*

We'll connect a sample dataset to a semantic layer, define key business entities and relationships, and demonstrate how Fabric IQ uses that ontological context to generate richer, more accurate insights. **Speaker**: Dean Jurecic is a solutions engineer and consultant who specializes in Microsoft Fabric and Power BI. He has worked with Power BI and Fabric in a variety of industries including utilities, retail, construction, government and education. Dean is an active member of the data community, a Microsoft Fabric Certified Data Engineer and Analytics Engineer Associate and a 3x Fabric Community Super User.

**Sponsor:** For almost 20 years, Wiiisdom has helped customers by providing first-class Analytics Governance Solutions that enable organizations to automate their analytics operations. The Wiiisdom Cloud Platform for Power BI and Tableau consists of 3 modules: Continuous Certification, Lifecycle Management and Predictive Monitoring that are designed to help you move from reactively to proactively managing your analytics estate.

If you have a skill set that can add value to our mastermind, come and visit us. We would love to meet you! One visit allowed per person. If you love us we will take a vote. If voted in you will become a valuable member of a game changing group.

long_description:
Here's the agenda for this Meetup:

Please note we will start promptly at 12:00 pm. Please be a few minutes early so you will have time to order some lunch. Also, give yourself a few minutes to catch up with other members. This will ensure that we can start on time and then we will be able to leave on time.

We do ask that as we get back to in-person networking, you WILL NEED to buy lunch to support Rock Bottom, there will also be a $1 restaurant service fee (that is NOT part of the gratuity) added to all checks.

• We'll do a brief introduction of ABNG and also quickly go over our rules (don't worry, there's only three and a half!). Then, we'll get right to the meeting.

• Hold on to your business cards for now. We will start the meeting by going around the room with our introductions. Notice we didn't say 30-second commercial or elevator pitch. There's a fantastic TED talk (https://youtu.be/u4ZoJKF_VuA) from Simon Sinek that might blow you away.

• After introductions, we'll do our shoutouts and share our member events. If you had a great 1:1 with someone or have some other awesome thing to share, we have the space for that! If you have a workshop, class, meeting or event coming up, this is a great time to inform the group. We will also discuss specific needs you may have. Do you need a resource of some kind? Chances are someone in our group can point you in the right direction.

• If time allows, we will engage in our Mastermind discussion. If you feel like you have something in your business that is holding you back, this is time and the place to tackle it. If you have something that you need help with, make sure to let the host know before the meeting starts so that we can make time for it during our meeting. The power of the group is immense!

• We'll close out our meeting by passing around business cards and ensuring you have time to set up your 1:1's before adjourning at 1:00 p.m.

We look forward to seeing you at our next meeting!

**Date:** Wednesday, August 5, 2026

**Key objectives we'll explore**

* Structure design presentations around the audience, problem, decisions, and outcome.
* Explain complex design work without overwhelming people with unnecessary details.
* Present ideas with greater clarity, confidence, and influence.

* Choose a project, concept, or design decision to present.
* Build a focused narrative with a clear beginning, middle, and conclusion.
* Practice presenting your story and gather feedback from other participants.

You will leave with a practical approach for developing stronger design narratives and presenting your work more effectively to clients, leaders, and cross-functional teams.

* Greater confidence explaining your process and decisions.
* Practical feedback you can apply to future presentations.

long_description:

Explore the path of Vajrayana and Great Perfection (Dzogchen)

Online classes, meeting twice a month, students will discover how to understand the pivotal principles of Tibetan Buddhism, make sense of empowerments, and go deep into understanding oneself, one’s own world, and how to make better sense of one’s own mind.

Vajrayana Training is offered in modules. The courses are non-sequential and can be taken in any order.

The Classes generally include a 30-minute lecture by Pema Khandro followed by 30-minutes discussion.

-fuel your inspiration
-discover your hidden depths
-immerse yourself in dharma
-connect with other Buddhists
-cut through fictions to see yourself as you really are
-understanding your mind and emotions
-gain support for ongoing practice and study
-clarify the meaning of esoteric Buddhist philosophy, terms and rituals
-engage Buddhist philosophy to grapple with the issue of teacher student relationships in Vajrayana
-leave behind the maze of information and have a direct encounter with the heart of Buddhism

What is Vajrayana?

Vajrayana is a Buddhist path for utilizing our life experiences as the fuel for the path. Vajrayana is a system of practices to cultivate a wakeful clear presence and connect with goodness in ourselves and others.

In Vajrayana ordinary life experiences become the focal point for our training. Vajrayana refers to a path of “transformation” of these experiences. It is the transformation of thinking, experiencing emotions, embodied experience, visualization, identity, moments of crisis, dreaming and dying into opportunities for connecting with intrinsic wisdom.

The view of the world in Vajrayana is that innate wisdom and potential for awakening is always present. Through Vajrayana meditation practices and Buddhist philosophy, we train to see the world with a “pure view,” an openness to connect with what is good, uplifted, the positive potential. long_description:
**The Art of Hands-On Adjustments & Assists**

Join us for an informative and experiential workshop designed for yoga teachers, teacher trainees, and dedicated students who wish to deepen their understanding of hands-on adjustments and assists. Rooted in the traditions of Astāṅga Yoga, skillful adjustments can help students experience greater alignment, stability, awareness, and ease within a posture while supporting the development of a safe and effective practice.

This workshop will explore the principles behind effective assisting, including proper body mechanics, communication, observation skills, and the distinction between adjusting, assisting, and supporting. Participants will learn how to assess individual needs, apply appropriate levels of pressure and guidance, and offer adjustments that enhance rather than force a posture.
We will work through a wide range of postures from the standing, seated, and reclining sequences, as well as techniques for supporting students in relaxation and Śavāsana. Emphasis will be placed on maintaining the integrity of the pose, honoring individual differences, and cultivating confidence and sensitivity as an assistant.
Whether you are a teacher looking to refine your hands-on skills or a student curious about the role of adjustments in yoga practice, this workshop will provide practical tools, hands-on experience, and a deeper appreciation for the art of assisting others on the yoga path.

\*Yoga Alliance YACEP accredited hours available

long_description:
Come out and join us for this exciting talk by Ben, and networking during the meetup and at the Burns Pub afterward.

Food will be sponsored by Sovereign this month. Learn more about sovereign at [https://sovereign.trading](https://sovereign.trading).

\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-

TL;DR: This talk is a primer for `std::execution`. Not just recipes, but understanding the computational model of senders.

C++26 adds senders to `std::execution`: a major feature that gives us tools for defining and composing asynchronous work. This talk will look at parts of `std::execution` and explain how they work, and how they map on to computational ideas.

We will deconstruct the ideas of execution; see how the familiar synchronous model fits in; see how the asynchronous model generalizes it; and get an understanding of how to build back up into anything we need. We'll cover all the major new parts of `std::execution`, and see the designs behind what ships in C++26 and where they might be fleshed out in future.

C++ has long been considered a low-level language in the sense of "close to the hardware". Now, arguably, it is finally becoming a low(er)-level language in a computational sense.

\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-

There is a discord for the meetup that you can join https://discord.gg/98T5XPWcrA to help foster remote interaction!
We always plan to go to the Burns pub for social hour after the presentation.

\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-

long_description:
**Sierra Club and Beer: Traveling through the Ages at Petroglyph National Monument**

*Sign up @ https://www.riograndesierraclub.org/calendar/*

Petroglyph National Monument, encompassing Albuquerque's West Mesa, encapsulates the human and environmental experiences from upwards of 20 million years ago to the present. With over 24,000 petroglyphs, primarily inscribed by the ancestors of modern Puebloan Peoples, the national monument preserves one of largest concentrations of petroglyphs in the world along with the desolate New Mexican High Desert's beauty.

This presentation, from Petroglyph National Monument's Community Volunteer Ambassador, Wes Reinig, is intended to highlight the incredible geology, environment, Ancestral Puebloan and Spanish culture and lifestyles that has dramatically changed over the course of the Albuquerque Area's rich and lengthy history. The importance of this monument operated by the National Park Service and City of Albuquerque is an ode to the land's historic usage and appearance in contrast with the rapid development of Albuquerque.

Come enjoy drinks and snacks with likeminded friends. RSVP at
*Sign up @ https://www.riograndesierraclub.org/calendar/*

The meeting will be held at St. Mark’s Episcopal Church, 431 Richmond Place NE, Albuquerque, from 7:00 p.m. to 8:30 p.m.

long_description:
In one of the most important and beloved Latin American works of the twentieth century, Isabel Allende weaves a luminous tapestry of three generations of the Trueba family, revealing both triumphs and tragedies. Here is patriarch Esteban, whose wild desires and political machinations are tempered only by his love for his ethereal wife, Clara, a woman touched by an otherworldly hand. Their daughter, Blanca, whose forbidden love for a man Esteban has deemed unworthy infuriates her father, yet will produce his greatest joy: his granddaughter Alba, a beautiful, ambitious girl who will lead the family and their country into a revolutionary future.

The House of the Spirits is an enthralling saga that spans decades and lives, twining the personal and the political into an epic novel of love, magic, and fate.

The program moves through the classical tradition with intention and heart: from the weight of a full-throated khayal to the playful intimacy of a thumri, and culminating in an original composition that reflects Swati's own voice within the lineage she carries.

Trained in the Indore and Mewati gharana traditions, Swati brings to the stage a rare ability to hold depth and warmth in equal measure.

She will be accompanied by **Tushar Gupte on tabla** and **Satyam Bagwe on harmonium**.

An evening of music in its most honest form.

**Swati Jhaveri** pursues music with a deep passion. She is currently under the guidance of Pandit Hemang Mehta (disciple of Padma Vibhushan Pandit Jasraj and Pandit Chandrasekhar Swamy) of the Mewati Gharana and Vidushi Kankana Banerjee of the Indore and Mewati Gharana (disciple of Ustad Amir Khan Sahib and Pandit Pratap Narayan) as part of the guru shishya parampara.

Swati started learning music at the age of 4 and has had the opportunity to study with many learned gurus including Pandit Pratap Narayan, Pandit Askaran Sharma, and Pandit Sougata Banerjee.

She started a non profit called “Swara Institute for Music Research and Appreciation” with the purpose of improving the reach of Indian Classical music through teaching, content creation, and supporting under-privileged, retired, and upcoming musicians.

Swati has produced a series of classical singles with a contemporary touch on popular platforms, in an attempt to make classical music palatable to wider masses and our younger generation.

long_description:
Everyone has something they can teach!

Join me for a fun, interactive Chinese meetup where participants are the teachers. No matter your level, from complete beginner to native speaker, you're invited to share something in Chinese with the group.

Your presentation can be as short as five minutes or as long as you'd like. You might bring a Chinese news article for us to read together, tell a story, teach us about a holiday or cultural tradition, share a favorite song, demonstrate a hobby, explain a grammar point, introduce new vocabulary, play a game, or teach us something completely unique, all in Chinese.

The goal is not to be a perfect teacher. It is to practice Chinese in a relaxed, supportive environment while learning from one another. Everyone has unique experiences, interests, and knowledge that can help the group grow.

Whether you come to teach, learn, or both, you will leave having practiced your Chinese in a meaningful and engaging way.

All levels are welcome. Bring your curiosity, your creativity, and something you would love to share. I'm excited to learn from you! I'll bring something short to share as well. Feel free to bring snacks for the group! ❤️

long_description:
Space is limited to 12. Please use this link to save your spot...[Sign me up!](https://forms.gle/xY3kf9ERwgAD7ptu8)

Let Your Fascia Flow is a 2 hour workshop incorporating Self-Myofascial Release techniques and Yoga to release tension, alleviate pain, and improve mobility.

Why Fascia Matters: Fascia is a web-like connective tissue that surrounds every muscle, bone, organ, and nerve and gives the body support and structure. It can be affected by physical injuries as well as our emotions. Physical injuries, surgeries and emotional strain in the body can lead to adhesions in the fascia which cause tightness, discomfort, pain and restricted movement.

Why you will love this workshop: Through targeted pressure, intentional movement and breath work, self-myofascial release aids in reducing fascial adhesions and tension, eases pain while promoting better movement throughout your entire body. Maintaining our mobility and range of motion is one of the keys to aging gracefully.

Perfect for you if: you're an athlete, weekend warrior, navigating mid-life changes, experiencing chronic tension, or simply looking to improve your overall well-being.

No previous yoga experience is required, just bring your curiosity and willingness to try something new!

What you will experience:

Guided self-myofascial release techniques using therapy balls and massage balls.
A series of yoga poses designed to stretch and open the body
Breath work and mindfulness to support relaxation and healing
Personalized adjustments to address your unique needs

Leave feeling lighter, more mobile, and deeply connected to your body.

title: iRest® Yoga Nidra - SECOND SUNDAY with Danielle Morris - ONLINE & IN-PERSON
description:
We are currently offering this session IN-PERSON at OM3 Yoga and ONLINE.

organizer: Come Sit With Us - A Meditation and Community Group
long_description:
Join us for a special community screening of *One Track Heart: The Story of Krishna Das*, followed by a conversation with director Jeremy Frindel.

The film follows the journey of Jeffrey Kagel, who leaves behind the possibility of a conventional music career and travels to India in search of something deeper. There, he encounters Neem Karoli Baba, known lovingly as Maharaj-ji, and begins a path that eventually leads him to become Krishna Das, one of the most beloved voices in modern kirtan and devotional music.

At its heart, this is a film about longing, heartbreak, devotion, music, and the search for what is real. It speaks to the ways life can break us open, the teachers and moments that change us, and the mystery of finding our way home through love.

After the screening, Jeremy will join us for a conversation about the film, the journey behind it, and the themes it opens up. There will also be space for community reflection and questions.

You do not need to know anything about kirtan, yoga, Hinduism, or meditation to attend. Come as you are.

**What to Expect**
We’ll gather, watch the film together, and then have a relaxed conversation with Jeremy Frindel. The space will be open, respectful, and rooted in the spirit of community. There is no pressure to share.

**[Please RSVP here](https://www.eventbrite.com/e/one-track-heart-the-story-of-krishna-das-screening-conversation-tickets-1993547622604?aff=oddtdtcreator)**

long_description:
Experience Marathi Magic at Asen Mee Nasen Mee in Dallas
Mark your calendar for the 13th of August, 2026 as Five Dimensions Entertainment 2026 proudly presents Asen Mee Nasen Mee in Dallas. This is more than an event, it's a celebration of Marathi culture and theatre, filled with drama and comedy. Shubhangi Gokhale, the star of the show, will take you on a journey through traditional Marathi narratives, humor, and emotions. Get ready for a memorable evening in the heart of Plano, Texas.
Meet the Star - Shubhangi Gokhale
Shubhangi Gokhale, born on 2nd June 1968, is a renowned name in Indian Marathi and Hindi theatre, film, and television. With her late husband, Mohan Gokhale, she has graced the screens in various roles, including the popular play Sakhar Khallela Manus. Currently, she is enchanting audiences with her performances in Colors Marathi's Raja Ranichi Ga Jodi and Zee Marathi's Yeu Kashi Tashi Me Nandayla. Her talent and expertise in the field of drama make her an artist of great appeal and relevance. Don't miss the chance to witness her perform live.
Discover the Grand Center
The Grand Center, located at 300 Chisholm Place in Plano, Texas, United States, is all set to host this exciting event. Known for its safety and accessibility, the venue offers a convenient and comfortable experience to its guests. Parking facilities are available, and the venue is surrounded by numerous Indian restaurants to satisfy your cravings for authentic Indian cuisine. So, come and enjoy the show in this dynamic location.
Secure Your Seats Now!
The tickets for Asen Mee Nasen Mee in Dallas are available in different levels to suit your convenience. Choose from $60 Level at $60.00, $50 Level at $50.00, $40 Level at $40.00, or $30 Level at $30.00. Grab your tickets now and ensure your participation in this unforgettable cultural extravaganza.

long_description:
**This event is posted on behalf of the Westerly Land Trust. Registration is required outside of Meetup. [Please register here.](https://www.eventbrite.com/e/paddle-yoga-float-flow-registration-1993347180075)**

Certified yoga teacher, Janice Fifer, will guide us through Sun Salutations with a focus on hip and shoulder openers to prepare for a paddle up the Pawcatuck River. We will stop along the way for a short meditation and ride the river’s gentle current back to the put-in point. The day will end with relaxation and a closing circle. This is a moderate paddle for kayakers with some experience, with the emphasis on relaxing and enjoying nature.

**What to bring:** BYO Kayak, Paddle board, canoe etc, Paddle, Life Jacket, Yoga Mat, Large Towel (to put under your yoga mat), Water, Bug Repellent. Be aware that your shoes will get wet and muddy.

**Please note:** Rhode Island State Regulations require that everyone, regardless of age, MUST wear a US Coast Guard approved life jacket, fastened in the manner the manufacturer intended.

**Parking:** Parking is available at Flora Whitely Preserve at [197 Potter Hill Rd](https://www.google.com/maps/place/197+Potter+Hill+Rd,+Westerly,+RI+02891/@41.4137429,-71.7974699,21z/data=!4m5!3m4!1s0x89e5dd6e2199da8f:0xd825c68fe1fa552!8m2!3d41.4136666!4d-71.797423?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI2MDYyOS4wIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D "https://www.google.com/maps/place/197+Potter+Hill+Rd,+Westerly,+RI+02891/@41.4137429,-71.7974699,21z/data=!4m5!3m4!1s0x89e5dd6e2199da8f:0xd825c68fe1fa552!8m2!3d41.4136666!4d-71.797423?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI2MDYyOS4wIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D"). We will put in for our paddle there as well.
This event is **FREE** for members, and $10 per person for not-yet members. Not a member and would like to be? [CLICK HERE](https://westerlylandtrust.org/support-our-work/make-a-gift/ "https://westerlylandtrust.org/support-our-work/make-a-gift/")!

**BAPS Detroit Mandir 22nd Patotsav (Anniversary)**

Celebrate the 22nd anniversary of the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in the Detroit area, beautifully coinciding with India's Independence Day.

This grand celebration will feature:

- **2:00 PM** – Vedic Mahapuja (sacred fire ceremony)
- **2:00 – 5:00 PM** – Annakut Darshan (offering of hundreds of food items to the deities)
- **4:00 PM** – Patotsav Sabha (cultural assembly with addresses by visiting swamis)

The Patotsav marks the sacred anniversary of the mandir's murti pratishtha (consecration of the deities) and is one of the most auspicious events of the year.

**Details:**
- Date: Saturday, August 15, 2026
- Location: BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Canton, MI
- Admission: Free and open to all

Special prasad and celebrations throughout the day. All families welcome.

long_description:
This book club is still forming! If you're interested, get on the waitlist and I'll be in touch. Note that dates / times / location may change.

**A woman’s desperate flight from an Apache raid unfolds into a sweeping tale of the Mexico–US border wars.**

Orchestrated with a stunningly imagined cast of characters, both historical and purely fictional, *Now I Surrender* radically recasts the story of how the West was “won.” In the contested borderlands between Mexico and the United States, a woman flees into the desert after a devastating raid on her dead husband’s ranch. A lieutenant colonel in service to the fledgling Republic, sent in pursuit of cattle rustlers, discovers he’s on the trail of a more dramatic abduction. Decades later, with political ambitions on the line, the American and Mexican militaries try to maneuver Geronimo, the most legendary of Apache warriors, into surrender. In our own day, a family travels through the region in search of a truer version of the past.

Part epic, part alt-Western, *Now I Surrender* is Álvaro Enrigue’s most expansive and impassioned novel yet. It weaves past and present, myth and history into a searing elegy for a way of life that was an incarnation of true liberty—and an homage to the spark in us that still thrills to its memory.

long_description:
Tech Talk:
**What Makes a Good Host: The Art and Science of Choosing a Website Platform in an AI Future**

We are bringing back our tech talks. This next session with be with Kate Kight

**Who is Kate:**
Kate is a creative technologist who believes in the power of design to solve problems and bring people together. From national brand identities to customized CRMs for local nonprofits, Kate creates scalable solutions designed to look good and do good.

**What to expect:**
A few years ago, it was almost impossible to believe the era of drag-and-drop websites would ever come to an end. But as major platforms wall in their tech stacks, hike prices, and cram in AI features to justify the cost, it’s time to explore alternatives. While AI can't replace human strategy, it can unlock cheaper, more scalable web hosting options with fewer tradeoffs.
Drawing on her expertise in crafting scrappy solutions for growing startups, Kate will share hands-on frameworks for selecting the right website builder, knowing when to hire a specialist (and whether you need a designer, developer, or business strategist), and scaling sustainably. You’ll walk away with actionable tools to avoid tech debt and build a digital foundation that grows with your business.

long_description:
**Date:** Wednesday, August 19 5:30-7:00 PM
**Venue:** Boise Main Co-Working Space (2210 W. Main St., Boise ID)
**Speaker:** Kelly Knopp (Creative Director, 116 & West)

What does it actually take to build a long, sustainable career in creative work today?

In this candid and unfiltered session, Kelly Knopp shares hard-earned lessons from decades in the trenches of advertising, design, and marketing. This is not a highlight reel. It’s the real story. The wins, the frustrations, the brutal truths, and the mindset shifts that separate those who last from those who burn out.
Drawing from a wide-ranging career across agencies, brands, and industries, Kelly breaks down what creatives often get wrong. From confusing assumptions with insight, to chasing “cool” instead of effectiveness, to struggling with communication, criticism, and relevance in an AI-driven world.

You will walk away with a clearer understanding of what actually matters:

* Why unspoken expectations kill projects and relationships
* The difference between ideas and ideas that actually land
* How emotion drives behavior and why that matters more than tools
* What it takes to stay relevant as the industry evolves
* The reality of rejection, pressure, and long-term growth in this field

This is a talk for anyone serious about doing meaningful creative work. Whether you’re just starting out or years into your career, expect a perspective check and a few uncomfortable truths that will make you better.

long_description:
Sacred Dialogs is a guided inquiry circle exploring the spiritual philosophy of the Bhagavad Gītā as a foundational yoga text (Yoga Śāstra) and a practical guide for conscious living.
Rather than a lecture format, the session uses Community of Inquiry methods inspired by philosopher Matthew Lipman, creating a respectful, thoughtful space where participants explore questions together.

Topics may include:
• Purpose and meaning in yogic life
• The nature of the self and consciousness
• Action, intention, and inner freedom
• Applying yoga wisdom to modern daily life

Participants are encouraged to listen deeply, reflect honestly, and share at their own comfort level. No philosophical background is required—curiosity and openness are enough. Each gathering concludes with a wholesome vegetarian dinner, allowing conversation to continue informally while fostering warmth, connection, and community. Donations welcome.

Join us for a night of laughter and drama at the Marathi play, "Asen Mee Nasen Mee" in Portland on August 21st, 2026. Her phenomenal performances in plays like Mohan Rakesh's Adhe Adhure, Shankar Shesh's Mayavi Sarovar, and Willie Russell's Educating Rita have won her immense acclaim. Don't miss the chance to see her live performance at our event!

The event is set to unfold at the HECSA BALAJI TEMPLE, located at 6100 Southwest Raab Road level 2, in the vibrant city of Portland, OR, United States. Known for its grand architecture and serene atmosphere, the venue is perfect for an evening of cultural immersion. It is easily accessible with ample parking facilities. After the show, you can explore nearby Indian restaurants to complete your cultural experience. Your safety is our priority, and the venue is located in a secure neighborhood.

long_description:
**A 90-minute vinyasa flow journey in the fresh air of the Wasatch mountains**

Drop into meditation, move through a full vinyasa flow, and then drape a cool lavender towel over your eyes for an extended savasana.

**Saturday, August 22nd 9:30-11:00 am @ Brighton Ski Resort**

You’ll already be up the canyon, so bring a friend and a picnic for a hike! It’s a ready-made self-care day ❤️

**Reserve a spot with a donation (recommended: $15-25)**
Venmo @emcapito with the “Brighton August” and your email for updates, and you are absolutely welcome to just show up!

**This is a community offering, so if the budget is tight or it’s your first time and you’d prefer to decide if you’d like to donate after, everyone is invited!**

* Suitable for all levels.
* Bring your own mat, water and sunscreen/sunglasses.
* Dress in layers – Utah weather is unpredictable!
* I also recommend socks just in case your mat gets hot in the sunshine.
* Ages 12 and up. Minors must have a parent/guardian present.

**Plan travel time so that you have at least 10 minutes to settle in.** The canyon always takes a little longer than expected. Give yourself a cushion and enjoy the beautiful drive.

**DIRECTIONS:**
Map: https://goo.gl/maps/f3ffkpHRvF2GtVce7
Brighton is at the top of Big Cottonwood Canyon. We will meet on the patio on the back of the Milly Chalet, which is the first building on your right as you turn into the large Brighton parking lot. It’s one level and cream colored next to a lift.

**Questions? Lost?** Text 801-898-0842

**Many thanks to Brighton Resort** **for hosting us over the years!**

If you have a screenplay that feels stuck or you are just looking for ways to tighten your narrative structure, join us for our next screenwriting workshop in Sheffield. This session is designed to be a practical, collaborative space where we look at the mechanics of plotting and how to keep a story moving effectively from the first act to the final fade out. We will spend part of the time discussing common structural pitfalls and the rest of the session working through specific plot points for projects you are currently developing.

Experience the Magic of Indian Classical Music Live!
Music enthusiasts are cordially invited to the grand spectacle of the "Pure Indian Classical & Semi Classical Ft. Kaushiki Chakraborty Live Concert" held on the 20th of September, 2026. Set in the heart of Washington DC, this melodic evening promises to be a journey through the enchanting realms of Indian Classical and Semi-Classical music. The concert offers a rare chance to witness the live performance of renowned artist Kaushiki Chakraborty, a gem of the Indian music scene. This event is a must-visit for lovers of Hindi music and live concerts.
About Kaushiki Chakraborty: The Reigning Queen of Indian Classical Music
The star of the evening, Kaushiki Chakraborty, is an acclaimed Indian classical vocalist hailing from the illustrious Patiala gharana. Born on 24th October 1980, Kaushiki's musical journey was guided by her father, Ajoy Chakraborty. Her music education at the Sangeet Research Academy has honed her skills, making her one of the leading exponents of Khyals and 'semi-classical' Thumris. She has been recognized globally, bagging the 2005 BBC Radio 3 Awards for World Music in the Asia-Pacific category. Kaushiki's performances with her husband Parthasarathi Desikan are known for their soulful renditions and harmonious chemistry.
Immerse Yourself in Melodies at Washington DC
The concert is set to take place in the bustling city of Washington DC, District of Columbia, United States. The venue offers excellent safety and accessibility, ensuring a comfortable experience for all attendees. For those seeking a complete Indian experience, numerous Indian restaurants are dotted around the venue, offering a delightful culinary experience.

title: BMW Dallas Marathon 2026
description: Dallas's premier marathon weekend with full marathon, half, ultra, 5K, and relay options. Benefits Scottish Rite for Children.
long_description: The BMW Dallas Marathon has been a Texas running tradition for over 40 years. The race weekend features a full marathon, half marathon, ultra marathon, 5-person relay, 10K, and 5K — something for every runner. The course starts at Dallas City Hall, loops through scenic White Rock Lake, and finishes back downtown. Since 1997, the marathon has donated nearly $5 million to Scottish Rite for Children. The December timing provides cool running weather, and the event has sold out three consecutive years.
venue_info: Start/finish at Dallas City Hall, 1500 Marilla St. The course is flat and fast, passing through downtown Dallas and around White Rock Lake (120m total elevation gain). DART light rail serves the City Hall area. Post-race party with food, beer, and live music.

title: San Diego Tamil Sangam Annual Membership 2026
description: Experience the Vibrance of Tamil Culture at the San Diego Tamil Sangam Annual Membership 2026
long_description:
Experience the Vibrance of Tamil Culture at the San Diego Tamil Sangam Annual Membership 2026
Mark your calendars for December 31st, 2026, as on this day, the San Diego Tamil Sangam will host its highly anticipated Annual Membership event. A cultural extravaganza that celebrates the richness and diversity of Tamil heritage, this event is a golden opportunity for Tamil enthusiasts to come together and revel in the vibrancy of this ancient culture. The event is sure to be a hub of engagement, enrichment, and entertainment that fosters the promotion and preservation of Tamil language, arts, and literature.
Artist: A Secret Yet to be Revealed
The event is yet to announce its artist, but it's known for featuring renowned individuals from the Tamil community who have significantly influenced the preservation and promotion of Tamil culture. The mystery guest, no doubt, will offer a memorable experience, showcasing the beauty of Tamil arts and literature that resonates with the audience and deepens their appreciation for this rich culture.
Immerse Yourself in Tamil Culture in the Heart of San Diego
The event takes place in San Diego, California, specifically at the 750 B Street location. The venue is in an easily accessible area of the city, known for its safety and proximity to a variety of attractions. After the event, guests can explore the city's vibrant nightlife, historical landmarks, and breathtaking beaches. And for those craving authentic Indian cuisine, there are numerous Indian restaurants nearby where you can indulge in a variety of flavorful dishes.
Secure Your Membership: Ticket Information
Various membership options are available for purchase, ensuring there's something for everyone. The Annual Family Membership is priced at $60.00, providing an excellent opportunity for families to be part of the Tamil community in San Diego. The Annual Individual Membership is available for $35.00, perfect for individuals passionate about Tamil culture. Additionally, the Student Membership from India is priced at a discounted rate of $10.00. For those who want to make a long-term commitment, the Lifetime Membership is available for $500.00. Make sure to secure your membership and be part of the San Diego Tamil Sangam's thriving community.
